title: Consumption-Aligned Reserve Credits and SLA Swapbook Pilot
text:
Consumption-Aligned Reserve Credits and SLA Swapbook Pilot

description:
Summary: Run a focused pricing & contract experiment that introduces 'consumption-aligned reserve credits' coupled with a tradable SLA credit ledger (the 'SLA Swapbook') for enterprise Dedicated customers. The goal is to make reserved GPU commitments more flexible for seasonal workloads while preserving predictable revenue and a clear SLA surface for ops teams. This ticket defines the experiment design, contract language variants, metric trackers, and implementation dependencies for a narrow pilot with 3 finance/ops-savvy customers.

Background & motivation: Customers frequently overcommit to reserved GPU capacity to avoid overage risk, then underutilize capacity for long stretches. Current rigid reserved models create churn friction and sales negotiation overhead. We want a variant that aligns committed spend to consumption patterns, offers burst/autoscale protection, and provides an insurance-like guarantee through SLA credits that are transferrable across reserve lanes.

Proposed constructs: 1) Consumption-Aligned Reserve Credits (CARC): customers buy time-windowed credits redeemable against Dedicated GPU throughput. Credits expire on a predictable cadence (monthly/quarterly) unless rolled into a grace pool. 2) SLA Swapbook: a ledger where SLA credits (e.g., for p95/p99 latency misses, preemption events, or capacity shortfalls) are recorded as tokenized credits that customers can apply to future invoices or trade for burst capacity within the same org. 3) Preemption Insurance Add-on: paid coverage that reduces the customer's exposure to preemption by allowing automated fallback routing to compatible model variants or regional capacity with SLA credit settlement.

Hypotheses: - H1: CARC reduces effective overcommit rate by at least 18% for customers with >30% seasonality compared to static reserved plans. - H2: Offering an SLA Swapbook that can be used as invoice credit will increase acceptance of flexible reserve tiers by >25% among enterprise pilots. - H3: Preemption Insurance reduces support escalations for bursting events by 40% for pilot customers.

Success metrics (pilot-level): - Reduction in reserved idle utilization (target 18% reduction). - Incremental ARR from pilot packaging (target $75k/quarter across 3 pilots). - Number of swapbook trades settled / month (target >= 4). - Support incident rate during bursts (target -40% vs baseline). - Legal & security signoff time reduced by 20% vs bespoke revisions.

Experiment plan: 1) Pricing SKU design: define three CARC sizes (Light / Standard / Heavy) with explicit credit-to-GPU-hour conversion, expiry, and grace-roll rules. 2) Contract language variants: (A) Invoice-credit swapbook with no cash refunds, (B) Swapbook allowing one-time convert-to-burst for small cash settlement, (C) Full refund guarantee with extended term (high commitment). 3) Billing & instrumentation: wire up telemetry to measure credit issuance, redemption, remaining credit %, swapbook ledger entries, and preemption events. 4) Pilot rollout: recruit 3 anchor accounts (target verticals: gen-AI platform, customer support analytics, and multimodal ingestion) for a 3-month pilot. 5) Legal & Security: produce SQ responses and a templated MSA addendum capturing swapbook accounting, data residency, KMS references, and preemption escalation playbook.

Operational considerations: - Console UX: a dedicated 'Credits & Swapbook' widget in the Console showing active credits, redemption history, and pending swap offers. - Billing integration: map CARC usage to invoice buckets; allow programmatic redemption via API. - Observability: new charts for reserved utilization, credit burn rate, and swapbook settlements. - Fallback behaviors: define default model-variant fallbacks to satisfy preemption insurance claims.

Risks & mitigations: - Revenue leakage from overly generous conversion rules -> conservative conversion rate with post-pilot adjustments. - Complexity in customer understanding -> one-page cheat-sheet and sales training. - Legal ambiguity on swapbook value -> clearly disallowed cash refunds in base variant and legal-approved accounting language in pilot contract.

Stakeholders: Sales (Michael Torres), Solutions Eng (Priya Rao), Legal (Nora Li), Finance (Aiden Murphy), Engineering (SRE lead: Casey Nguyen), Console PM (Jules Marquez).


acceptance_criteria:
SKU definitions published and approved by finance and sales
Three pilot customers signed on variant A or B and instrumented
Swapbook ledger implemented in billing backend and visible in console mockups
Telemetry capturing credit issuance/redemption and preemption events with dashboards
Draft MSA addendum and SQ answers completed and reviewed by legal

comments:
2026-03-04: Initial concept presented at PM sync. Positive feedback, need clearer billing model.
2026-03-06: Solutions Eng flagged requirement for per-tenant ledger isolation; added to dependencies.
2026-03-09: Finance ran early sims; recommended smaller credit granularity to reduce rounding noise.
2026-03-12: Legal requested explicit language prohibiting secondary-market sale of swapbook credits outside the org.
2026-03-14: Engineering feasibility call: estimated 3 sprint effort for backend ledger + 2 sprint for console UX prototypes.

notes:
Keep default CARC expiry conservative (monthly) to make behavior predictable for customers and accounting.
Expose API to allow programmatic redemption by customer orchestration systems.
Pilot should include one customer willing to trial variant C (refund-like option) to stress-test financial impact under controlled cap.
Track churn propensity for customers who convert from static reserves to CARC over a 6-month window.
